goal: Prevent loss of commanded braking torque
fsr: The braking controller shall detect inconsistent brake actuator feedback and request the defined degraded mode within 100 ms.
tsr: The feedback monitor shall compare commanded and measured torque every 10 ms and flag a mismatch lasting 50 ms.
test: Inject missing actuator feedback and verify degraded-mode request within 100 ms.
rationale: S3, E4, C3 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

fsr: The braking controller shall reject a brake torque command that fails plausibility checks within 100 ms.
tsr: The command monitor shall check range and pedal correlation every 10 ms.
test: Inject an out-of-range torque request and verify command rejection within 100 ms.
rationale: S3, E4, C2 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

hazard: Increased steering effort and contact with obstacle
goal: Maintain controllable steering during assistance loss
fsr: The steering controller shall indicate assistance loss to the driver within 500 ms.
tsr: The diagnostic monitor shall detect missing assist motor feedback within 100 ms.
test: Disconnect motor feedback and verify driver indication within 500 ms.
rationale: S1, E4, C1 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

fsr: The steering controller shall disable assistance on a confirmed torque plausibility fault within 50 ms.
tsr: The torque monitor shall compare two independent sensor channels every 5 ms.
test: Inject a torque sensor disagreement and verify assistance disable within 50 ms.
rationale: S3, E4, C3 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

goal: Prevent acceleration without valid driver demand
fsr: The propulsion controller shall limit torque on an accelerator sensor disagreement within 100 ms.
tsr: The pedal monitor shall compare redundant pedal channels every 10 ms.
test: Inject pedal channel disagreement and verify torque limitation within 100 ms.
rationale: S3, E3, C3 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

hazard: Loss of acceleration while exposed to traffic
goal: Preserve a controlled transition on propulsion loss
fsr: The propulsion controller shall provide a loss-of-propulsion warning within 300 ms.
tsr: The drive monitor shall detect commanded torque without measured drive response within 100 ms.
test: Suppress drive response during a simulated overtake and verify warning within 300 ms.
rationale: S2, E3, C2 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

hazard: Reduced road visibility and obstacle collision
fsr: The lighting controller shall command available redundant illumination and issue a warning within 200 ms after a lamp fault.
tsr: The lamp monitor shall check current feedback every 20 ms.
test: Disconnect a headlamp in the night scenario and verify fallback command within 200 ms.
rationale: S3, E3, C2 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

fsr: The lighting controller shall activate the available brake lamp channel within 100 ms of a valid braking request.
tsr: The brake lamp monitor shall diagnose an open circuit within 50 ms.
test: Inject an open brake lamp circuit and verify alternate-channel activation within 100 ms.
rationale: S2, E4, C2 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

hazard: Overcurrent due to erroneous electronic control
goal: Prevent excessive charging current caused by a control fault
fsr: The battery controller shall request charge isolation within 100 ms of a confirmed overcurrent control fault.
tsr: The current monitor shall compare sensor readings with the configured synthetic current limit every 10 ms.
test: Inject an invalid charging command and verify isolation request within 100 ms.
rationale: S3, E2, C3 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

hazard: Sudden propulsion interruption and collision risk
fsr: The battery controller shall reject a contactor-open command without a valid fault or shutdown condition.
tsr: The contactor monitor shall verify command authorization and state feedback every 10 ms.
test: Inject an unauthorized open command and verify it is rejected.
rationale: S2, E4, C2 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

hazard: Driver lacks speed feedback and overspeeds
goal: Provide a visible indication of speed signal loss
fsr: The cluster shall display a speed signal fault within 1000 ms of invalid speed data.
tsr: The communication monitor shall mark a speed signal invalid after 200 ms without a valid update.
test: Drop speed messages and verify fault display within 1000 ms.
rationale: S1, E3, C2 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.

scenario: Low speed reversing near a pedestrian
hazard: Collision with a pedestrian behind the vehicle
fsr: The reverse assistant shall suppress invalid distance values and indicate unavailable assistance within 200 ms.
tsr: The sensor monitor shall reject distance values that fail configured plausibility checks.
test: Inject a false-clear distance value and verify unavailable-assistance indication within 200 ms.
rationale: S2, E3, C2 are authored demonstration inputs for this specific event; they have not been established by field evidence or expert approval.
